title: 2026 UK ETS maritime delegated-responsibility QA controls

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme for maritime: how to comply

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS

facts.source_fact: A maritime operator can be the registered owner or an ISM company that has taken responsibility for ship operation, ISM compliance and UK ETS compliance under a legally binding written agreement.
facts.expected_handling: Require all applicable responsibility elements before assigning operator status.

facts.source_fact: Delegation of UK ETS responsibility can only take effect on or after completion of the legally binding written agreement and cannot be backdated.
Where a delegation agreement sets a future commencement date, the Environment Agency should be notified.
facts.expected_handling: Keep future-effective delegation distinct from current responsibility.

facts.source_fact: A non-registered-owner operator must provide registered-owner contact details and complete the delegated-responsibility declaration in METS.
facts.expected_handling: Require METS declaration evidence for delegated ships.

facts.source_fact: Termination or a material change to the delegation agreement must be notified to the Environment Agency within 14 days by varying the relevant monitoring-plan section in METS.
Delegation for a ship not already in the monitoring plan is a significant change requiring a plan variation and related declaration.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat a newly delegated ship as a minor metadata edit.

facts.source_fact: If the regulator has not identified the responsible person, the registered owner is treated as the maritime operator.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the registered-owner fallback only when responsibility has not otherwise been identified.

facts.source_fact: Where operator responsibility changes during a scheme year, each entity has obligations only for the period in which it meets the maritime-operator criteria.
facts.expected_handling: Split responsibility by effective date and period.

facts.source_fact: An ISM company does not become the maritime operator merely by operating the ship and complying with the ISM Code if UK ETS responsibility has not also been legally delegated.
facts.expected_handling: Do not infer ETS responsibility from ISM status alone.

facts.source_fact: Maritime operators have legal UK ETS obligations and non-compliance can lead to civil penalties.
facts.expected_handling: Treat responsibility determination as a compliance boundary, not an informational label.

guard_patterns.handling: Forbid backdating and preserve effective date.
Check operation, ISM and UK ETS responsibility elements.
Treat new delegated ship as significant variation.
Allocate obligations only to responsible periods.
Do not derive vessel emissions from responsibility records.

generation_rule: CARTESIAN_PRODUCT facts x guard_patterns; 10 x 10 = 100 controls
